evals.prompt: I want to change the grafana skill, where do I edit? Do not run anything; tell me the exact steps and commands.
evals.expected_output: Says to run scripts/skill_origin.py grafana first, explains that its output names the scope, the source repo, its policy and the clone path, and directs the edit into that clone. Never suggests editing the installed folder under .agents/skills or an agent's own skills folder.

expectations.text: Tells the user to run skill_origin.py on the grafana skill as the first step

expectations: Explains that the skill_origin.py output identifies the scope, the source repo, its policy, and the clone path where the edit belongs
Directs the edit into the source clone, not into the installed folder
Does not suggest editing the installed skill folder directly as the way to change the skill

evals.prompt: Fix a typo in my be-honest skill. `skill_origin.py be-honest` printed: scope project (CLI flag: none); source my-skills [direct-push]; source url git@example.com:me/my-skills.git; ref (default branch); clone /work/my-skills; agents (-a) agent-a agent-b; result CLEAN; autonomy auto. The clone has no AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or CONTRIBUTING.md, and I have no rules of my own about commits or pushes. Do not run anything; tell me the exact steps and commands.
evals.expected_output: Edit be-honest inside the clone /work/my-skills, validate with npx skills add /work/my-skills -l, run the conflict check (autonomy auto, no convention files, no session rule: no conflict), state in one line what will happen, then commit and push the default branch without asking for approval, refresh with npx skills update be-honest -p -y from the project root, and verify with skill_origin.py be-honest. No feature branch, no PR.
expectations: Says to edit the be-honest folder inside the clone /work/my-skills, not the installed copy
Says to commit and push the default branch directly, and treats this as a no-conflict case: it does not make commit or push wait on the user's approval

expectations.text: Refreshes the project-scope install with update and the -p flag

expectations: Does not use the -g flag for this project-scope skill
Does not tell the user to create a feature branch or open a pull/merge request
Mentions checking for a convention/autonomy conflict before the first commit, or states why there is none here

evals.prompt: Add a new skill called release-notes-writer to my my-skills repo (direct-push, clone /work/my-skills, url git@example.com:me/my-skills.git, its other skills are installed globally, agents agent-a agent-b). Do not run anything; tell me the exact steps and commands.
evals.expected_output: Create release-notes-writer/SKILL.md in the clone with name: and description: frontmatter where name equals the folder name, add the index row if the repo keeps one, validate with npx skills add /work/my-skills -l, commit and push the default branch, then install once with npx skills add git@example.com:me/my-skills.git -g -s release-notes-writer -a agent-a agent-b -y because update never adds a new skill.
expectations: Says SKILL.md needs name: and description: frontmatter and that name must equal the folder name
Says to validate with npx skills add <clone> -l before pushing
Says to commit and push the default branch (no branch or PR)

expectations.text: Installs the new skill by name, globally

expectations: States that npx skills update never installs a new upstream skill, which is why the explicit add is required

evals.prompt: Add a gotcha to the o11y skill. `skill_origin.py o11y` printed: scope global (CLI flag: -g); source team-skills [branch-then-review]; source url https://git.example.com/team/team-skills.git; ref (default branch); clone /work/team-skills; default branch main; agents (-a) agent-a agent-b; autonomy auto. evals.expected_output: Sync the clone to main, create a branch, edit the o11y skill folder, validate, run the conflict check (none here), commit and push the branch without asking, install from the branch with the #branch suffix and -g, ask before opening the PR/MR against main, and after the merge re-add from the default branch to clear the pinned ref.

Says to make the edit on a new git branch and push that branch without waiting for approval (no conflict here), then open a pull/merge request against main, asking the user before opening it

expectations.text: Shows a branch install command using the #<branch> suffix on the repo URL

expectations: Says that after the merge the skill must be re-added from the default branch to clear the pinned ref
Does not tell the user to push directly to main

evals.prompt: My skills PR got merged and the branch was deleted. The skill (deploy-sop, global, from team-skills) was installed from that branch while in review. Anything left? Do not run anything; tell me the exact steps and commands.
evals.expected_output: Yes: the lock entry is pinned to the deleted branch, so updates skip the skill (at global scope without even a failing exit code). Re-add it from the default branch with npx skills add <url> -g -s deploy-sop -a <agents> -y, plus any other pinned-ref skill from that source, then confirm with skill_origin.py that no pinned-ref remains.

expectations.text: Says to re-add the skill with npx skills add from the default branch

expectations: Explains that the lock entry is pinned to the branch ref and that once the branch is deleted, updates stop refreshing the skill

expectations.text: Says to verify with skill_origin.py that the pinned ref is cleared

expectations: Does not say nothing is left to do
The re-add command installs from the default branch: its URL carries no #branch suffix

evals.prompt: Tweak the wizard skill. `skill_origin.py wizard` printed: scope project; source public-skills [read-only]; clone (none). I also have a direct-push source my-skills (clone /work/my-skills, url git@example.com:me/my-skills.git). Do not run anything; tell me the exact steps and commands.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to edit the installed folder because the source is read-only. Fork: copy the installed wizard folder into /work/my-skills under a new name, set name: and description:, push the default branch, npx skills add git@example.com:me/my-skills.git -s <new-name> -a <agents> -y at project scope, then remove the original with npx skills remove wizard -y (no -a list), verify, and start a new agent session.
expectations: Refuses to edit the installed wizard folder in place, explaining that an update would overwrite it
Says to copy the skill into the my-skills clone under a new name, not the same name wizard
Explains the reason for a new name: lock entries are keyed by name so a same-named fork would fight with the original

expectations.text: Removes the original with npx skills remove

expectations: The remove command does not pass an -a agent list, or the answer explains that passing -a leaves the files and lock entry behind
Says to start a new agent session afterwards

evals.prompt: Install the retro skill from https://github.com/some-author/skills. My config agents are agent-a agent-b. Do not run anything; tell me the exact steps and commands.
evals.expected_output: First list what the repo offers with npx skills add https://github.com/some-author/skills -l, check skill_origin.py --all for a name collision, settle the scope (asks, or follows where that source's other skills live), then install with one -s and one -a: npx skills add <url> <scope-flag> -s retro -a agent-a agent-b -y, and add a read-only entry for the source to the config.

expectations.text: Lists the repo contents first with the -l flag before installing
Install command uses -s retro and the configured agents

expectations: Addresses which scope (project or global) to install at, by asking or by stating the rule used, instead of silently assuming one
Mentions checking for a name collision before installing, or adding the new source to the config as read-only

evals.prompt: The acme-cli skill looks outdated. `skill_origin.py acme-cli` printed: policy externally-managed; placed by acme binary (acme skills install); refresh with: acme upgrade. Do not run anything; tell me the exact steps and commands.

expectations: Says explicitly not to use npx skills add, update, or remove on acme-cli
Says the missing lock entry is by design and that acme-cli is not an orphan and should not be deleted

evals.prompt: skill_origin.py --all says deploy_sop (global) is deleted upstream and renamed to deploy-sop, which is already installed. What do I do? Do not run anything; tell me the exact steps and commands.
evals.expected_output: Remove the old name: npx skills remove deploy_sop -g -y (no -a list), verify with skill_origin.py deploy_sop that it is no longer installed, and start a new agent session so the old description leaves the routing table. Update will not remove it when run by an agent.

expectations.text: Removes deploy_sop with npx skills remove at global scope

expectations: The remove command does not pass an -a agent list
Says to verify the removal afterwards
Says to start a new agent session afterwards so the old description stops loading
Does not tell the user to run npx skills update as the way to remove the old skill

evals.prompt: I just installed manage-skill on a new laptop. I ran skill_origin.py --all and it exited with code 3 saying there is no config. What now? Do not run anything; tell me the exact steps.
evals.expected_output: Explains this is the first run: the config lives at ~/.config/manage-skill/sources.json and must be created with the user. Run init_config.py --discover from the project root, then for each source ask whether the user can push and whether the default branch is protected (read-only / direct-push / branch-then-review), ask for clone paths, the agents, and who owns each unlocked folder, show the JSON, get a yes, pipe to init_config.py --write, then --check and skill_origin.py --all.
expectations: Says the policy for each source is decided by asking the user (can you push; is the default branch protected or reviewed), not guessed

expectations.text: Writes the config through init_config.py --write after the user confirms

expectations: Names the config location ~/.config/manage-skill/sources.json or the MANAGE_SKILL_CONFIG override
Does not invent sources, clone paths or policies on the user's behalf

evals.prompt: I'm in my project folder, which has a skills-lock.json. I also have global skills. Give me the one command that refreshes all my global skills. Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: npx skills update -g -y. Explains that the scope flag is required: a bare npx skills update run non-interactively in a folder with project skills updates the project scope only, without saying so.

expectations.text: Gives npx skills update with the -g flag

expectations: Explains that without -g or -p the CLI picks a scope on its own (project here), so the flag must always be passed

evals.prompt: skill_origin.py --all lists tdd under NAME COLLISIONS: installed from public-skills; scope global+project. Is that a problem, and what do I do? Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: Yes: the same name is installed at both scopes, so two copies load and can drift. The user should choose which scope to keep; remove the other with npx skills remove tdd (with -g for the global one, no flag from the project root for the project one), without an -a list, then verify and start a new agent session. The agent does not pick for the user.
expectations: Explains that the skill is installed at both project and global scope and therefore loads twice
Leaves the choice of which install to keep to the user instead of picking one

expectations.text: Shows the remove command for tdd

expectations: The remove command does not pass an -a agent list

evals.prompt: Fix a typo in my deploy-sop skill. `skill_origin.py deploy-sop` printed: scope global (CLI flag: -g); source ops-skills [direct-push]; autonomy auto; source url git@example.com:ops/ops-skills.git; clone /work/ops-skills; default branch main; agents (-a) agent-a agent-b; result CLEAN. The clone's AGENTS.md contains the line: "Agents must never run git push without the maintainer's explicit approval." Says the push lands on the default branch.
expectations: Identifies the AGENTS.md rule as a conflict that requires asking, even though autonomy is auto
Quotes or clearly cites the AGENTS.md rule in the question it would ask
Asks once for the whole commit-push-reinstall loop (approve for the session, or gate each step) rather than planning a separate prompt at every step by default
Does not say it would commit and push without asking

expectations: Says it would ask the user before the first commit because the source's autonomy is ask
The question covers the whole loop (commit, push, reinstall) once, not a separate approval per step by default

expectations.text: Refreshes the project-scope install with update and -p

expectations: Mentions that a description change only shows up in a new agent session
